title: “He Hath Borne Our Griefs, and Carried Our Sorrows”

sparks.section: Jesus Christ took upon Himself my sins and sorrows.

cards.text: Movie heroes win by crushing the bad guy. Isaiah's Savior wins by carrying our pain Himself.
Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.
Centuries before Jesus was born, Isaiah described a Savior who would be despised and hurt. He frees us by taking our place: our sins, and also our sadness and grief.
Read Isaiah 53:4–6 again, swapping "we" and "our" for "I" and "my," and notice how it feels.

sparks.reflectPrompt: What's something heavy you'd be willing to let Him help carry?

gameSparks: With his stripes we are healed.
The Lord wants you to come home.
His ways are higher than ours.
Seek the Lord while He may be found.
phraseMeaning: Jesus Christ didn't only pay for sins. Isaiah says He took on our griefs and sorrows too, so we never have to carry them alone.
